topic.title: Understanding the actual task
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
In the commercial world, this is called “understanding your customer.” ChatGPT is quite good at doing market research.

I looked more closely at the competition description and focused on the phrase “natural product structures” from mass spectra. I then asked ChatGPT to investigate what Enveda is really interested in.

does this look familiar to our 3 class of test set??

Here are some Enveda papers/resources you should not miss:

  1. Butler et al., “MS2Mol: A transformer model for illuminating dark chemical space from mass spectra.” Their goal is de novo prediction of natural metabolites that are not present in existing databases.
    They also introduced EnvedaDark, a benchmark of 226 natural products that were absent from major databases.

  2. MS2Prop: A machine learning model that directly predicts chemical properties from mass spectrometry data for novel compounds.

  3. PRISM, Enveda’s current foundation model: https://enveda.com/news/pr-enveda-biosciences-announces-microsoft-collaboration-and-reveals-foundation-model-to-read-and-translate-chemistry/

  4. https://www.bruker.com/en/landingpages/bdal/customer-insight-enveda.html

  5. https://pubs.acs.org/jnprdf/article/89/9/2436/5428694/Chemotaxonomic-Map-of-Labdane-Diterpenoids-in
    example of dark chemical prior
    "timsTOF is the combination of high-resolution MS + fast MS/MS + ion mobility, which fits complex natural-product profiling very well."

There is much more information available. It may be worth asking your AI agent to research Enveda’s papers, platform, and view of natural-product chemical space.

Some useful natural-product structure databases to investigate are COCONUT, LOTUS, and NPAtlas. The key point is that “natural product structures” may be a very important clue about the target distribution of this competition.

just my guess. take with a pinch of large grains of salt …
